meta.topic: Selling a used car: time to sell, listing fees, private vs trade-in gap, transfer paperwork
meta.method: WebSearch to locate, WebFetch (or curl with a browser user agent where WebFetch was refused) to read the publisher's own page. confirmed:true only where the figure or step was read on the publisher's own page. Search-engine summaries and third-party pages are recorded with confirmed:false and a note.
meta.caveat: Most published days-to-sell figures measure dealer stock, not private listings. Each entry says which.

privateVsTradeIn.source: Autotrader UK, citing the Money Advice Service
privateVsTradeIn.finding: Selling privately is often 10-15% more than selling to a dealer
privateVsTradeIn.note: Autotrader's own page, but the figure is attributed to the Money Advice Service (now MoneyHelper); the original MAS page was not read.

privateVsTradeIn.finding: Private Party Value exceeds Trade-In Value because the dealer pays reconditioning, safety inspection and other costs of doing business. KBB Instant Cash Offer is a real offer valid 7 days, redeemable at participating dealers.
privateVsTradeIn.note: KBB publishes no fixed percentage gap; the gap is per vehicle in its valuation tool.

privateVsTradeIn.finding: Private-party value is always higher than trade-in; trade-in is always the lowest of the values. No fixed gap published.
privateVsTradeIn.note: Search summary of Edmunds pages; edmunds.com returned 403. Forum anecdotes ($1,500-$2,000 over trade) are not a published figure and are not used.

privateVsTradeIn.finding: Instant offer valid 7 days; paid by bank transfer 30-60 minutes after signing. No comparison with private sale price published.

sellerSteps: Notify DMV within 5 calendar days of selling or transferring title and delivering possession (CVC §5900)
File the Notice of Transfer and Release of Liability online, or mail form REG 138
Provide: plate number, last 5 of VIN, new owner's name and address, odometer reading, make/year/description, sale date, seller's name and address
transfer.note: Page does not state a fee (search summaries say online filing is free) and does not address plates or smog in this section.

sellerSteps: Complete and sign the transfer-of-ownership section of the title certificate
Sign a Vehicle Bill of Sale (MV-912), even for a gift; it must show year and make, VIN, date of sale, purchase price, names and signatures of buyer and seller
For a gift, mark price $0 and complete Section 6 of DTF-802
Remove plates and the registration sticker before the sale; turn plates in at a DMV office unless transferring them to another vehicle
transfer.note: Plate step is from DMV search snippets of the same page set; the fetched page summary did not include it, so treat the plate step as confirmed:false.
transfer.buyer: New owner registers and titles at a DMV office

sellerSteps: Complete and sign the reverse of the certificate of title and give it to the new owner with a bill of sale (Form H-31)
Keep copies of the completed title and bill of sale
Remove plates and cancel the registration with DMV (online cancellation: print the receipt)
Keep liability insurance until the registration is cancelled
Vehicle stays subject to town property tax until the registration is cancelled; send the assessor the cancelled-plate receipt and bill of sale for a prorated bill
Give the buyer a Used Vehicle Information Package (UVIP), required under the Highway Traffic Act
Complete and sign the vehicle portion of the ownership permit and the Application for Transfer on its back
Give a signed bill of sale (names, buyer address, date, price, VIN, vehicle details); handwritten original accepted
Provide a Safety Standards Certificate if required
Keep the licence plates (plates travel with the driver)

fees.delivery: online orders mailed within 5 business days plus up to 10 days delivery; same day in person at ServiceOntario

sellerSteps: Remove licence plates
Tear off the bottom signed vehicle registration portion of the APV250 and give it to the buyer
Complete and sign all four pages of the Transfer/Tax Form (APV9T)
Take both to an Autoplan broker, ideally together with the buyer, so the seller's name and insurance are removed from the record
Cancel insurance or transfer it to a new vehicle
transfer.note: Seller may display the plates on a substitute vehicle of the same class for up to 10 days (from ICBC search snippet, confirmed:false).

sellerSteps: Tell DVLA online to change the registered keeper (service hours Mon-Fri 7am-9pm, Sat-Sun 7am-8pm); DVLA sends a log book to the new keeper
Cannot use online if the V5C was already posted or there is no log book
Without a log book, write to DVLA, Swansea SA99 1BA with seller name/address, registration, make and model, exact date of sale, and new keeper's name and address
Vehicle tax is cancelled on notification; refund for any full remaining months
Buyer must tax the vehicle (or SORN) before driving; tax does not transfer
transfer.note: Online service needs the 11-digit V5C reference (search summary). No statutory deadline or fee stated on the page.

transfer.authority: Department of Transport (NVDF), via Citizens Information and motortax.ie
sellerSteps: Change of ownership must legally be registered; it is free of charge
Online (motortax.ie): seller enters the registration and VRC number; a one-time transfer PIN is emailed to the owner's NVDF email address
Seller shares the PIN with the buyer; it expires after 30 minutes
Buyer enters the PIN, logs in with verified MyGovID, accepts a declaration; a new VRC is posted to the buyer; date of sale is the date processed online

By post: seller and buyer both sign the change-of-ownership section on the back of the VRC; send to the Department of Transport (Vehicle Registration Unit, Shannon); about 2-5 days to process once received
Selling to a dealer: give the dealer the VRC; both complete Form RF105; approved dealers can notify online, otherwise seller posts RF105
Buyer can only tax the vehicle once the change is processed
transfer.note: Until the change is notified the seller stays the legal registered owner and is liable for fines (motortax/council pages, via search). Citizens Information is a State information body, not the Department itself.

steps: Buyer (new owner) applies for cambio de propietario within 15 working days
Appointment through SEMOVI online system with a Llave CDMX account

Requirements: valid official photo ID, CDMX proof of address, proof of tenencia/refrendo payments for the current and prior applicable years, tarjeta de circulación, document proving ownership (factura)
transfer.note: Both CDMX official pages (cdmx.gob.mx and semovi.cdmx.gob.mx) refused connection; all figures from search summaries of those pages and third-party guides (reported range $417-$433 MXN for 2026).
